pr.title: Give the Projects page's columns the same widths in every status
pr.head: 7a3bd6f7198ed2048bef7f3ad0ca53621f6950c4

summary: The Projects page on a repository's Projector site lists every project plan, grouped by status: in-progress, ready, draft and completed. Each status is its own HTML table with the columns Project (the plan's title), Priority, Owner and Name (the project's path under docs/projects/). Owner shows only when some plan names an owner.

Each table sized its columns to its own rows, so a status whose titles were shorter, or whose names were longer, put Priority, Owner and Name at different horizontal positions from the status above it. The page read as four unrelated tables rather than one list.

This change gives every status's table the same fixed column widths, the approach the site's Reviews index already uses. The title column takes the remaining width and wraps. In a window 760px wide or narrower, the Name column is hidden, because the title already links to the project. That is the same width at which the site moves a section's sidebar above its page, and it keeps the title wider than Name wherever Name shows.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Fixed table layout: with CSS table-layout: fixed, the browser takes column widths from the <col> elements and the first row only, never from the content of later rows.
  • <colgroup>: an element at the top of a table that holds one <col> per column, which CSS can give a width.
  • Nested project: a plan inside another plan's directory, such as alpha/beta. Its title cell is indented by depth.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• The first head hid Name at 640px. Its review was clean, with one suggestion: between 641px and about 700px the title column was no wider than Name, so most titles wrapped to three lines.
  • The second commit moves the breakpoint to 760px, the sidebar's breakpoint, and the test now checks that the two match.

groups.title: Every status table gets the same columns
groups.kicker: The Projects view writes a colgroup and marks the Name column
intro: showProjects in site/src/site.ts draws the Projects view: one table for each status, in the order STATUS_ORDER gives. Each table now opens with a <colgroup> whose <col> elements carry the classes priority, owner and name, and the header row moves into a <thead> with the project rows in a <tbody>.

The Name header and cells also get the class name, so one CSS rule can hide the column on a phone. The same owners flag adds both the Owner <col> and the Owner header and cells, so the colgroup always has one <col> per column.
site/assets/site.js is the compiled output of site.ts, which the repository commits.

files.note: The Projects view's table markup gains a colgroup, a thead and tbody, and a name class on the Name column.

checks.text: Every status's table gets the same colgroup. A site built from this head and rendered in headless Chromium at 1200, 761, 760, 700 and 375px puts each heading at the same left offset and width in every status's table.
The nested-project indent stays as inline padding-left on the title cell. Under a fixed layout it shrinks the title's text area, not the column, so nesting never moves the other columns.
The filter box still works: it selects tr[data-search], and the rows inside the new <tbody> keep that attribute. A fixed layout also keeps the column widths steady while the filter hides rows.
npm ci, npm run check and npm run build in site/ pass, and the build leaves this file byte for byte as committed.

groups.title: The stylesheet fixes the widths
groups.kicker: A fixed layout, three column widths, and a phone breakpoint
intro: site/assets/site.css sets table-layout: fixed on the projects table and gives each <col> its width in em, which the table's 14px font turns into pixels. Because a fixed layout ignores cell content, a long owner or name can no longer widen its column. overflow-wrap: anywhere on every cell makes such a value wrap instead of overflowing, at a hyphen where it has one and anywhere when it has none.
The owner cell loses white-space: nowrap, which would otherwise keep a long login from wrapping.

At 760px or narrower, a media query hides every element with the class name (the <col>, the header, and the cells) and narrows the Owner column to 6em. The site already stacks a section's sidebar above its page at that width, in the @media (max-width: 760px) rule near the top of the file. The Reviews table uses the same hiding pattern for its time column, at its own 640px breakpoint.

files.note: The projects table's fixed widths, wrapping, and phone rule.

checks.text: At 760px, 700px and 375px, the Name header and cells render as display: none, Owner measures 84px, and neither the page nor any table wrapper scrolls sideways. That held with a 30-character hyphenated login, a 39-character slug with no hyphens, and projects nested three deep.

At 761px, with every column shown, the title column measures 315px beside a 15px classic scrollbar, or 330px with an overlay scrollbar. That is well over Name's 196px. At 760px the title column measures 538px.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The markup tests follow the new header, and one test covers alignment
intro: ProjectsViewTests renders the Projects view in Node and asserts on the HTML. The two existing tests now expect the colgroup and thead. A new test, test_every_status_table_sets_the_same_column_widths, renders three statuses and checks that their colgroups are identical, that a nested row keeps all four cells with its indent in the first, and that site.css carries the fixed layout, the three widths and the 760px rule, and that the sidebar's own rule uses the same 760px breakpoint.

checks.text: The full suite passes at this head under Python 3.12: 531 tests.
